Figure 1:Comparison of 3D CoCa, 3D CoCa v2, andour 3D CoCa v3.Previous methods focus on indoor 3D scene understanding through contrastive learning, generative captioning, and test-time search.
Our framework extends this paradigm to urban scenes with geometry-aware multi-view representations, MSG-based relational descriptions, and question-guided multimodal decoding.

Figure 2:Construction pipeline of City3D-9.6K.(a) Multi-view RGB images and point maps are rendered from urban point clouds, with corresponding view-level captions generated by Qwen.
(b) Multi-view scene graphs (MSG) associate shared entities and spatial relationships across viewpoints, providing structured context for scene-level caption generation.

Figure 3:Overview of 3D CoCa v3.The framework learns geometry-aware representations from multi-view RGB images and XYZ point maps through Scene-CLIP contrastive pre-training, complemented by MSG-derived relational descriptions.
A multimodal decoder subsequently integrates question-relevant scene captions and projected visual features into a LoRA-adapted Qwen backbone for urban 3D question answering.

Figure 4:Qualitative comparison on City-3DQA under the city-wise split.We compare 3D CoCa v3 with representative baselines on single-hop and multi-hop questions involving object counting and spatial relationships.
Our method correctly answers all four questions in the illustrated unseen urban scene.

Figure S3:Additional qualitative comparisons on City-3DQA under the city-wise split.We compare 3D CoCa v3 with representative baselines on multi-hop and single-hop questions using multi-view RGB observations, point clouds, and corresponding XYZ point maps.
Green checkmarks and red crosses indicate correct and incorrect predictions, respectively.
Ground-truth (GT) answers are provided for reference.

Figure S4:Additional qualitative comparisons on City-3DQA under the sentence-wise split.The examples focus on multi-hop questions involving object counting, functional relationships, and spatial reasoning.
We compare predictions from different methods against the ground-truth (GT) answers.
Green checkmarks and red crosses indicate correct and incorrect predictions, respectively.

Figure S5:Additional qualitative results on urban functional understanding.Examples illustrate multi-hop and single-hop questions involving functional object counting, including educational, retail, residential, cultural, and governmental facilities.
The predictions of 3D CoCa v3 consistently match the ground-truth (GT) answers.

Figure S6:Additional qualitative results on urban spatial relationships.Examples demonstrate multi-hop reasoning about relative accessibility and spatial relationships among administrative, commercial, and residential areas, together with localized object counting and facility identification.
3D CoCa v3 correctly answers all illustrated questions.

Figure S7:Additional qualitative results on fine-grained spatial reasoning.Examples involve spatially localized object counting, relative distance comparison, and facility existence in urban scenes containing office spaces and temporary structures.
All predictions of 3D CoCa v3 are consistent with the ground-truth answers.

Figure S8:Additional qualitative results on urban relational reasoning.Examples illustrate relative accessibility, spatial proximity, object counting, and facility existence involving marketplaces, public administration buildings, and commercial areas.
3D CoCa v3 correctly answers all illustrated single-hop and multi-hop questions.
